author: TheloVely
quote:
13 years in the making and 80 bucks later, I must say, this game is exactly what's wrong with modern gaming. A game that punishes you for having fun, stops you from killing NPCs the same way you could in any other GTA title, and down right stripped the game of things that were in every other one before it. Rockstar is showing such disrespected to the players that have played their games since GTA 3. Let's break it down. 
1 - 30 FPS: The idea that this game is locked in 30 FPS in consoles, for the sake of realistic graphics, shows that Take Two and Rockstar are leaning heavily on the Movie Game style of design that has been plagging the market ever since TLOU was a huge success.
2- The Added Mechanics: A karma level was added, just like in Red Dead Redemption 1 and 2. The problem is that in those games, it made sense for the karma to exist, because the whole point of the games is to go on a REDEMPTION journey. GTA isn't that. It has never been that. GTA 6 is the only game I've ever seen that punishes a player for landing headshots, because killing people in this game is bad, and you're supposed to simply maim them. How noble. They made stealing vehicles a pain, in a GRAND THEFT AUTO game. The new wanted system is not needed, period. And to top it all off, no spoilers, but just like in RDR2, your actions lead to different consequences, which in a GTA game, a game about being a cold blooded bastard, doesn't work well.
3- The Writing: It's not as good as GTA 5, 4 or San Andreas. It's not as good as Red Dead Redemption 1 or 2. It's the exact type of writing that has you slugging through it, because you paid 80 bucks for this game, and Rockstar refuses to refund, so might as well force your way to the end. 
4- Attempting to Erase GTA's Legacy: The game stops you from killing NPCs around town, in bars and in random events, because i guess it would be fun, and we can't have that. No more prostitutes. They dumbed down the strip teasing to simply watching, when in GTA 5 you could do much more, if you know you know. The franchise that is known as THE gangster simulator, is suddenly trying to shove the moral weight of committing crimes and doing wrong things down players throats.
5- Fitness: They brought working out back. I will say, i really liked working out on GTA San Andreas. The difference is, in San Andreas, you got lean to get laid, you got fat to get laid, and you gained muscle to get laid. But in GTA 6, you're stuck with Lucia, who is a pain in the ass, and even if you let the relationship die, the game doesn't let you get anyone else.
6- The Protagonists: This is another case **** that was clearly made with a female protagonist in mind. But anyone with a brain cell knows that wouldn't sell, so they added Jason as a playable character as well. The same thing happened in AC Syndicate, and It's what's happening to the new Fable game. As GTA protagonists, Jason and Lucia are NOT it. Not even close. Jason is a good guy. A GOOD GUY. That's not GTA. Lucia is a woman, written by women. The type that Trevor Phillips would tell to shut the F up. That's not GTA.
7- Chores in a GTA: Why are you making me do stuff that I already do in real life in GTA? Groceries, maintenance, painting? IT'S GTA, Motherf*c***rs! A game where you build your base is one thing, but making a player do it just to make Lucia happy? Hard pass.
8- Game Feel: Games like this have a solid base when it comes to gameplay. But it does not feel any different from GTA 5. You got indie games making such amazing animations for every little different thing, but GTA 6 just feels like GTA 5, but new, if that makes any sense. Landing headshots still feels good, but like I said, the game punishes you for it. Driving is solid, but it's supposed to, because god forbid they manage to mess that up as well.

Another disgraceful sequel to a beloved IP. The amount of games like this keeps pilling on. I had hope that the same guys that made Bully would still be there, working at that studio, but I guess not. No point in coping. Use your 80 bucks for something else.
